items.title: Mozambique: Prevention of money laundering demands strengthening capacities to supervise DNFBPs
items.summary: According to Mendonça, speaking on the sidelines of a regional seminar on risk-based supervision currently being held in Maputo, supervise designated non-financial businesses and professions is also crucial in order to avoid the country’s return to the Financial Action Task Force (FATF) “grey list”, officially known as “Jurisdictions under Increased Monitoring The “grey list” includes countries identified by the FATF as having strategic deficiencies in their measures to counter money laundering and the financing of terrorism. Countries on this list are subject to increased monitoring and scrutiny by the FATF. The list is intended to serve as a warning to the countries concerned to improve their performance and comply with international standards Mozambique was included on the “grey list” in 2022. However, it was removed from the list on October 2025 during a plenary session of the FATF, held in Paris Mendonça explained that strengthening supervision to DNFBPs is part of preparations for the next international evaluation, scheduled for 2030.

items.title: Mozambique: Mining company reportedly closes road to Mavonde to extract gold – O País
items.summary: The road in question is the main access route to Mavonde, a region considered important for agricultural production in Manica district. With traffic interrupted, farmers and other road users are facing difficulties travelling and transporting produce and other goods Elias Djokonia has expressed concern about the situation, questioning how a mining operation was allowed to interfere with a public road “We are truly astonished. We are amazed by the Chinese company that closes the road, claiming that it wants to extract gold. And it puts the road out of use, and the alternative route will not be passable when it rains,” he said For his part, Tendai Hanguire, who has used the road for more than 30 years, said he was surprised by the interruption of traffic to make way for gold exploration and mining activities This is sad because they have closed the road we have been using since 1992. I have always driven here. This alternative route is in poor condition.

items.title: How AI giants could raise the cost of borrowing in Europe
items.summary: France, Germany and Italy face a volatile bond market as war inflation bites. With US tech giants now issuing billions in AI bonds, they are competing with cash-strapped European governments With more than $1 trillion (€900 billion) pouring into the artificial intelligence (AI) build-out, US tech giants are now competing with governments and companies in Europe for the same investment capital Four of the Big Five hyperscalers — Amazon , Google -owner Alphabet, Meta and Oracle — have issued around $250 billion in bonds in dollars since the beginning of 2025, according to a tally of filings to US financial regulators by AI Industry Reviews, an independent platform that evaluates AI tools. They have sold a further €37 billion ($41 billion) of bonds in euros Recently, Microsoft — the last of the Big Five to hold back — joined the AI borrowing spree with a $25 billion bond sale, all in dollars Next year, Goldman Sachs projects that total new AI hyperscaler bond sales are expected to reach $420 billion.

items.title: Agricultural Campaign Plan budgeted at 189.8 million dollars launched
items.summary: Maputo, 03 Nov (AIM) – Mozambique’s Agriculture Ministry on Monday launched 2026/27 Agricultural Campaign Plan budgeted at 189.8 million US dollars aimed at “transforming the agricultural sector through a sustainable increase in production and productivity, the integration of value chains and the strengthening of producers’ competitiveness, promoting the transition from subsistence farming to a market-oriented commercial sector.” The plan is funded by the World Bank, the African Development Bank and the International Fund for Agricultural Development (IFAD). In a statement, the Ministry’s explains that the plan was presented during an Agricultural Campaign preparation meeting chaired by Agriculture Minister Roberto Albino. The minister challenged managers of projects being implemented by the Ministry of Agriculture, to ensure that their interventions converge, so as to contribute to meeting the targets set for the 2026/27 Agricultural Campaign, in line with the private-sector-centred operational model. “The Plan is mandatory. We are no longer here to discuss it.

items.title: North Korea denies being behind record $6.3bn Binance hack

items.title: Uganda arrests former army deputy chief stripped of military rank
items.summary: Uganda accuses Peter Elwelu of stockpiling weapons and organising activities against the government Uganda has arrested former deputy military chief and presidential adviser Peter Elwelu over allegations of involvement in activities aimed at destabilising the country Acting military spokesman Chris Magezi said Elwelu, whom he described as a "renegade" officer, was arrested on Monday evening and would be charged in court The arrest comes days after Uganda's defence chief, Muhoozi Kainerugaba, announced that he had stripped Elwelu of his lieutenant general rank and demoted him to a private Elwelu has not commented on the allegations Elwelu rose to prominence in 2016 when he oversaw a deadly military raid on the palace of a regional king accused of leading a separatist movement. He was subsequently appointed army chief He later rose to become the deputy chief of defence forces before being named presidential adviser In May 2024, the US government imposed sanctions on him over alleged human rights abuses, including extrajudicial killings committed by government forces.
